**What I found:** Moving `src/orders/billing.js` into its own subsystem is reasonable, but the evidence that would justify it isn't available here, so don't move it yet (the record calls this DEFER). The weekly-change claim is an assertion, and this directory is not a git repository, so there is no history to show billing changing on its own; the complexity measurement a move needs (gate C) also hasn't been run.

**Why it matters:** If billing really does change on its own, separating it means weekly edits stop landing in orders, and the move is cheap to undo: `orders/index.js` is its only caller, it imports nothing, and no data has to migrate. If billing actually changes together with orders, moving it adds a cross-domain edge and fixes nothing.

**Do this first:**
1. Get the co-change history from wherever this code is version-controlled, e.g. `git log --since=6.months --name-only -- src/orders`. Billing changing in most weeks while `index.js` and `repository.js` stay still supports the move.
2. Run `/alchemy C` on the proposed move, then re-run `/alchemy L` to accept or reject it.
3. Decide whether the weekly change is in code or data. Today it is mostly in data: the `TAX` and `DISCOUNT_TIERS` tables at `src/orders/billing.js:3-7`. If that holds, moving the tables out of the code is smaller than creating a new subsystem.

**What I did not check:**
- Co-change history: `git log --name-only` in the repo that has the history.
- Structural complexity change: `/alchemy C`.
- Runtime flow, shared data and failure spread: no telemetry or incident data exists here.
- Declared positions and inbound interfaces: none exist in this repo (no `eslint.architecture.mjs`), so the domain check was judged from file layout only.

One thing I noticed outside L's scope: `placeOrder` (`src/orders/index.js:6`) never applies tax, and `reprice` (`src/orders/index.js:14`) updates the total but leaves the invoice stale. These may be bugs, and they're worth checking before billing moves.
